Tests that {@code withOverrides()} returns a new, distinct {@code Value} whose included-property set is the intersection of the base and the override sets.

Setup:

  • {@code overrideValue} — includes {@code {"$h]54GG#Ke5AZNb`7r"}}, ordered=null
  • {@code baseValue} — built from a mock annotation whose {@code value()} returns a one-element null array (yielding included={null}) and {@code order()} returns {@code OptBoolean.DEFAULT} (yielding ordered=null)
  • {@code mergedValue} — intersection of {null} and {"$h]54GG#Ke5AZNb`7r"} = {} (empty)

Because the two included sets are disjoint, the merged result is empty and therefore unequal to both the base and the override {@code Value}.
Override Value: includes exactly one specific property name
Base Value built from a mock annotation: value() → one-element null array ⟹ included set = {null} order() → OptBoolean.DEFAULT ⟹ ordered = null
The merged result is a newly created, empty-included Value — it must differ from both inputs by value and by reference
